newsitem.title: CHINA: Exports of Beijing foreign-funded ventures up.
newsitem.headline: Exports of Beijing foreign-funded ventures up.

text.p: Exports of foreign-funded ventures in China's capital rose in the first three months of 1997, while those of state enterprises slipped, the Beijing Economic Daily said on Saturday.
Exports of Beijing-based wholly foreign-owned enterprises and Sino-foreign joint ventures rose to $228 million in the first quarter, the newspaper said without giving the percentage increase.
Their exports soared a year-on-year 89 percent in January, 66.7 percent in February and 56.5 percent in March.
The first quarter figure accounted for 44.8 percent of the Chinese capital's total exports, it said.
Exports of foreign-funded firms were mainly to Japan, Hong Kong and the United States, consisting mainly of electronic products, garment, machinery, electrical and medical equipment.
Exports of Beijing-based state enterprises fell to $220 million in the first quarter, the newspaper said without giving comparative figures.

Their exports slipped by a year-on-year 30.7 percent in January, 24.3 percent in February and 15.2 percent in March, the newspaper said. Exports consisted mainly of garments, steel, machinery and cotton.
